entries.title: Acts 20:1
segments: When the uproar had ceased, Paul sent for the disciples, and, with encouraging words, bade them goodbye, and started on his journey to Macedonia.

entries.title: Acts 20:2
segments: After going through those districts and speaking many encouraging words to the disciples, he went into Greece, where he stayed three months.

entries.title: Acts 20:3
segments: He was about to sail to Syria, when he learned that a plot had been laid against him by the Jews; so he decided to return by way of Macedonia.

entries.title: Acts 20:4
segments: He was accompanied by Sopater the son of Pyrrhus, of Beroea, Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica, Gaius of Derbe, and Timothy, as well as by Tychicus and Trophimus of Roman Asia.

entries.title: Acts 20:5
segments: These men went to Troas and waited for us there;

entries.title: Acts 20:6
segments: While we ourselves sailed from Philippi after the Passover, and joined them five days later at Troas, where we stayed for a week.

entries.title: Acts 20:7
segments: On the first day of the week, when we had met for the Breaking of Bread, Paul, who was intending to leave the next day, began to address those who were present, and prolonged his address till midnight.

entries.title: Acts 20:8
segments: There were a good many lamps in the upstairs room, where we had met;

entries.title: Acts 20:9
segments: And a young man named Eutychus, sitting at the window, was gradually overcome with great drowsiness, as Paul continued his address. At last, quite overpowered by his drowsiness, he fell from the third storey to the ground, and was picked up for dead.

entries.title: Acts 20:10
segments: But Paul went down, threw himself upon him, and put his arms round him. "Do not be alarmed," he said, "he is still alive."

entries.title: Acts 20:11
segments: Then he went upstairs; and, after breaking and partaking of the Bread, he talked with them at great length till daybreak, and then left.

entries.title: Acts 20:12
segments: Meanwhile they had taken the lad away alive, and were greatly comforted.

entries.title: Acts 20:13
segments: We started first, went on board ship, and sailed for Assos, intending to take Paul on board there. This was by his own arrangement, as he intended to go by land himself.

entries.title: Acts 20:14
segments: So, when he met us at Assos, we took him on board and went on to Mitylene.

entries.title: Acts 20:15
segments: The day after we had sailed from there, we arrived off Chios, touched at Samos the following day, and the next day reached Miletus;

entries.title: Acts 20:16
segments: For Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus, so as to avoid spending much time in Roman Asia. He was making haste to reach Jerusalem, if possible, by the Festival at the close of the Harvest.

entries.title: Acts 20:17
segments: From Miletus, however, he sent to Ephesus and invited the Officers of the Church to meet him;

entries.title: Acts 20:18
segments: And, when they came, he spoke to them as follows: "You know well the life that I always led among you from the very first day that I set foot in Roman Asia,

entries.title: Acts 20:19
segments: Serving the Lord, as I did, in all humility, amid the tears and trials which fell to my lot through the plots of the Jews.

entries.title: Acts 20:20
segments: I never shrank from telling you anything that could be helpful to you, or from teaching you both in public and in private.

entries.title: Acts 20:21
segments: I earnestly pointed both Jews and Greeks to the repentance that leads to God, and to faith in Jesus, our Lord.

entries.title: Acts 20:22
segments: And now, under spiritual constraint, I am here on my way to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there,

entries.title: Acts 20:23
segments: Except that in town after town the Holy Spirit plainly declares to me that imprisonment and troubles await me.

entries.title: Acts 20:24
segments: But I count my life of no value to myself, if only I may complete the course marked out for me, and the task that was allotted me by the Lord Jesus--which was to declare the Good News of the Love of God.

entries.title: Acts 20:25
segments: And now, I tell you, I know that none of you will ever see my face again--you among whom I have gone about proclaiming the Kingdom.

entries.title: Acts 20:26
segments: Therefore I declare to you this day, that my conscience is clear in regard to the fate of any of you,

entries.title: Acts 20:27
segments: For I have not shrunk from announcing the whole purpose of God regarding you.

entries.title: Acts 20:28
segments: Be watchful over yourselves, and over the whole flock, of which the Holy Spirit has placed you in charge, to shepherd the Church of God, which he won for himself at the cost of his life.

entries.title: Acts 20:29
segments: I know that, after my departure, merciless wolves will get in among you, who will not spare the flock;

entries.title: Acts 20:30
segments: And from among yourselves, too, men will arise, who will teach perversions of truth, so as to draw away the disciples after them.

entries.title: Acts 20:31
segments: Therefore, be on your guard, remembering how for three years, night and day, I never ceased, even with tears, to warn each one of you.

entries.title: Acts 20:32
segments: And now I commend you to the Lord and to the Message of his Love--a Message which has the power to build up your characters, and to give you your place among all those who have become Christ's People.

entries.title: Acts 20:33
segments: I have never coveted any one's gold or silver or clothing.

entries.title: Acts 20:34
segments: You, yourselves, know that these hands of mine provided not only for my own wants, but for my companions also.

entries.title: Acts 20:35
segments: I left nothing undone to show you that, laboring as I labored, you ought to help the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said himself--'It is more blessed to give than to receive.'"

entries.title: Acts 20:36
segments: When Paul had finished speaking, he knelt down and prayed with them all.

entries.title: Acts 20:37
segments: All were in tears; and throwing their arms round Paul's neck, they kissed him again and again,

entries.title: Acts 20:38
segments: Grieving most of all over what he had said--that they would never see his face again. Then they escorted him to the ship.
